report.source_text: Renal tissue histology [Figure 3] on light microscopy showed marked mesangial cell increase, some of which contain apoptotic debris; significant features of acute tubular necrosis with simplification of tubular epithelial cells, some of which are cystically dilated containing amorphous eosinophilic material; and interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy in about 10–20% of the section examined. There was no increase in the mesangial matrix and thickening or duplication of the glomerular basement membrane. Features were in keeping with lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Lupus glomerulonephritis (International Society of Nephrology/Renal Pathology Society [ISN/RPS] Class II)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old female presented in September 2014 to renal outpatient clinic with body swelling and frothy urine while being managed for periodontal gingival cellulitis. Clinical examination revealed facial puffiness, jaw swelling, massive lower limb edema, and ascites. Laboratory evaluation demonstrated nephrotic syndrome (proteinuria 2.7 g/day, severe hypoalbuminemia 17.2 g/L), renal impairment (serum creatinine 167.3 umol/L, eGFR 42 ml/min/1.73m2), active urinary sediment (15-20 pus cells/hpf, dysmorphic RBCs, granular and epithelial casts), and serologic evidence of systemic lupus erythematosus (strongly positive ANA with homogeneous pattern, elevated anti-dsDNA 30 IU/ml). Systemic inflammatory markers included leukopenia (1.7 × 10^9/L), anemia (18%), and markedly elevated ESR (133 mm/1st hour). During admission, in the 3rd week, she developed hyperpigmented malar rash, gum hypertrophy, and bleeding with oliguria and rising serum creatinine. Renal biopsy light microscopy confirmed ISN/RPS Class II lupus glomerulonephritis, showing marked mesangial cell increase with apoptotic debris, acute tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis with tubular atrophy (10-20%), and absence of GBM thickening or duplication. She was treated with intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g daily for 3 days), followed by tapered oral prednisolone and mycophenolate mofetil (720 mg bid), along with dialysis for oliguria and uremia. After 6 months of treatment, significant clinical and biochemical improvement was documented: proteinuria reduced to 0.2 g/day, serum creatinine improved to 94 umol/L, eGFR rose to 82 ml/min/1.73m2, and ESR decreased to 44 mm/h.
